The Apostle spends this whole Chap. in answering this Object. and in our text and the following verses he Argues that the dominion abounding & Reigning of Grace it will have a directly Contrary tendency in those that Recieve it tha that the Gospel which so much is such di a dispensation of Grace instead of Encouraging sin tends to deliver from its Deliver from its in all that are heartily E Entertain it.

## 110. Job 31:3 110.Job 31'3 trans

Jonathan Edwards

Job 31 .3 ----------------- and a strange Punishment to the workers of Iniquity. Jobs three friends in their discourse with him under his afflic tion very much insisted upon it that he was not upright that he had secr notwithstanding all his profession of G & appearance of Godliness he yet Enter secretly Entertain'd some wickedness & Practiced some wickedness and that that was the Reason that he met with such aff troubles & Calamities that his Calamity was brought upon him as a punishment of his wickedness & hypocrisy

______________________________

Job on the other hand vehemently asserts his own Innocency Integrity & faithfullness . he he is upon this argument here in this Place. in the first verse of this Chapter he particularly asserts his purity from & freed Innocency with Respect to Unclean Practices. I made a Covenant ------------------------- in the 2 our text & the v. foregoing he Gives the Reason why [-] he thus kept him d did or what it was that made him afraid to Indulge his Lusts fleshly lusts. for viz because of Gods vengeance against wickedness what Portion of G. __________________________ This third verse is an answer to the Interrogation in the 2. v. there it is asked. what portion ------------ _____________ here he answers that destruction is to the wicked the i. e. is the portion of God from above to the wicked. and a strange Punish -------------- is the Inheritance of the Almighty from on high to the workers of Iniquity . and therefore he dared not to allow himself in any secret sin for says he in the next v. Doth he not see my ways & Count all my steps. That Punishment was more strange than than now not being so fully Revealed doc. That it is a strange Punishment [^010-note1] that G. has assigned to the Workers of Iniquity.

1. we shall show. what a that it is a strange -- 2. shall Enquire why G. assigns such a strange Punish. & then make appli.

## 114. Ps. 65:9 114.Ps. 65'9 trans

Jonathan Edwards

Ps. 65.9. -- Thou Greatly Enrichest it with the River of G. which is full of water ----------

___________

This Psalm seems to be written upon Occasion of some special mercies being shown to the Children of Israel after some Great Calamity & General Calamity . and by the latter Part it seems to have been the sending of Rain and Giving fruitfull seasons after some Great drought of or Famine . This mercy is Elegantly described in our text & the following verses. G He Enricheth the Earth with the River of G. that is full of water. that is G. never want water to supply the Clouds & to Pour upon the dry & thirsty Ground Gods River is alwaies full he Can when when he Pleases Cause the heavens to Yield a plentifull supply for the Earth God by of Causing it often to Rain upon the Earth the water is Continually from year to Year Comi from the beginning of the world Coming down upon the Earth but yet Gods River is not Empty but as full as ever. God wisdom has so Contrived for the Continual supply of the Earth and his Goodness so abundantly is so Abundant in it that it is like a River Ever flowing.

____________________________________

This is a beautifull Representation not only of Gods bounty in supplying Greatness. fullness & Constancy of Gods bounty in Giving Rain but also in other things [^014-note1] in the Yearly & daily mercies which he bestows upon us .

____________________________________________________

Prov 23. 5. Wilt thou set thine Eyes upon that which is not for Riches Certainly make them selves wings and fly Away as an Eagle towards Heaven. The wise man in these five first verses of the Chapter warns us against three things. viz excess in Gratify fying an the Animal appetite to meat & drink and a too Eagerly seeking Earthly Riches. and Ete Entertaining too high an opinion of our own wisdom or all may be Reduced to One viz a setting our hearts upon Earthly Vanities. He warns us especially to beware of an excess ive in an In dulgence of an appetite after meat & drink a In a time of temptation when thou sittest to Eat with the Ruler of thy People a Ruler Consider diligently what is before thee and Put a knife to thy throat if thou be a man Given to Appetite. Be not desirous of his dainties for they are deceitful meat one may Easily & unawares be deceived by that which so pleases the Appetite to Go to excess and a man had need to be as fear Carefull & man as fearfull Least as if he had a knife at his throat a man if he had a knife Pointed at his throat would be very wary Least he should be hurt by it so had a man need to be that is tempted with meat or drink that is very Pleasing to the appetite.

That this is no human or or Common Lovesong or is But a divine song Mystically Representing of spiritu al and divine things is many ways Evident. this One thing Indeed is Enough that it is one of those Books that was delivered down by the Church of the Jews with other Books of scripture divine authority as part of the Canon of the scripture. that it was Esteemed by them & used by them as such from the days of the Prophets and those Inspired teachers which that nation of old had amongst them . and was ap were in the Canon of the Old Testament and w in X time & the apostle times was one part of that which was called scripture then was never disapproved by them but was part of that book which X and the apostles meant when they spoke of the scripture as directing us to search the scriptures and when they said all scripture is Given by Inspiration & the like they meant the old Testament which the scriptures of the Jews as the Old Testament of which this was one book. but besides this there are many things in this song it self that Evidence that the it is no Common love song or & that they are not Common lovers that Are here spoken of as might be Particularly shown were there Ro Room for it here and here is nothing in this song the matter of this song disagreable to the divine Author supposed [^018-note1] divine author or divine subject but the similitudes here Used as Representing of X to a Lover or bride & the Church to Lovers Representing X to a bridegroom & the Church to a spouse are a Comparison a is very agreable to the manner of the scripture in many othe & there is the same Comparison made in Innumerable other Places. and Indeed the very Name of the song Confirms it viz. the song of songs Confirms it that it is a more than Ordinary Love song and that it was designed for a di vine song and is of divine Authority for we Read 1. Kings 4. 32 that solomons songs were a thousand & five . this he Calls the song of songs that is the most excellent of all his songs which it seems very Probable to be upon that Account because it was a song upon the most excellent subject treating of the Love Union & Communion between X & his spouse of which marriage & congugal love were but a shadow these were the most excellent lovers & this Love the most excellent love & therefore this song the most excellent song or the song of songs. II. What is Implied in J X the Peple of X Glorifying in X. To Glory is for a person to express his Esteem of his ownown Advantages of excellency honour or happiness above others .The word in the Original the text in the Original signifies to show forth ones own praise or to exalt ones self with ones own Praises . there therefore boasting or [^020-note7] Glorying is Generally taken in an ill sense as an expression of a haughty disposition thus when the Apostle when he [^020-note8] is setting forth the exceeding Great wickedness of the Hea then he mentions this amongst other things that they were boasters. Rom 1 . 30 self praise is spoken of as by the Wise man as a foolish thing Pro 27.2. Let another praise thee ---------------------- But there is one sort of Glorifying that is no manifestation of Pride but Rather the Contrary and is most Consistent with a wi Prudence. And but this one sort . 1 Cor [^020-note9] 1.31 Let him that Glorieth Glory in the L. The Act of Glorying in X Contains these.

at new place [----] preachd Math 7. 14. strait is the Gate and narrow is the way that Leadeth Unto life and few there be that find it These words are a part of Xs sermon on the mount the Greater Part of the ser foregoing Part of the sermon is taken up in Prescribing & Recommending Particular duties But X now drawing towards towards an End of this discourse Concludes with some more General directions, and Enforcements that Respect the whole of what he had said. as here Enter in at the strait Gate . which is as much as to say Observe and do these things which I have now Commanded you for tho it may seem to you a difficult & hard matter to Conform to Em Yet they are the way that Leads Unto life and the only way . for wide is the Gate. ------------------------------- if You will walk in Other ways that are not Conformed Give yourselves to live as by you life List and according as your Corruptions Carry you that is the way that Leads to destruction and Because strait is the Gate ---------------------------- But if you would walk in the way that Leads to life there is need of Your Utmost Care and Labour in order to it & self denial diligence and selfdenial in order to it more than the Greatest Part of those that seek Eternal life [----]. The subject of the Prosposition in the text is twofold 1 here is the Gate by which we Enter into life a Gate that must be Enter before Persons begin to live [^024-note1] a spiritual life and to be Entitled to Eternal life which Gate is Conversion. then 2. there is a way to be walked in after the Gate is Enterd before we Can arrive at that Crown & perfection of life which is the Principally Proposed to be sought by us the Object of our Pursuit which is a holy life a life of universal & Persevering Obedience to Gods Commands

In answer to this Objec I shall Endeavour to show how the terms of salvation may be said to very Easy & how they may be said to be very difficult . for it may be said very truly both ways the terms of salvation are very Easy in such as a sense as magnifies the wonder full Grace of G. to us in offering of it upon such terms we Cant think of any way wherin he Could have shown in his Grace more with Respect to the Easiness of the terms then he has done . they are also very Easy in all the way in such a sense as in all the ways that Rend a man foolish & in unreasonable & inexcuseable in not Complying . and Yet they are very difficult in such a sense as makes Great Care Labour & striving necessary in order to the Performance of them. therefore I answer. .

Eph. 5. 1. Be Ye therefore followers of G. as dear Children. . The Apostle in the Conclusion of the foregoing Chap been exhorting the Xtians he wrote to Put away all Bitterness, & wrath and Anger and Clamour & Evilspeaking with all malice and to be kind to one another tender hearted forgiving one another and Enforces the exhortati it by putting of them in mind of the wonderfull Kindness & mercy of G to them in forgiving them for Xs sake . there is Gods own example for them to follow. Be ye therefore says the apos. followers of G as dear Children. & as G. has forgiven you so do ye forgive others as G has been kind & Bountifull to you so be ye Kind one to another. and Gods Rewards have Earned towards you in your misery so be ye tender hearted one to another . as G. had hath expressed such an unparallelled love to you so be ye far from bitterness & wrath and anger & malice one towards another. Here we may take notice.

## 139. Num. 14:22-23 139.Num. 14'22-23 trans

Jonathan Edwards

Numb. 14.22.23. Because all those men which have seen my Glory and my miracles which I did in Egypt and in the wilderness & have tempted me now these ten times and have not hearkend to my Voice. surely they shall not see the Land which I sware unto their Fathers neither shall any of them that Provoked me see it. We have here in this Chap. an Account of the murmuring of the Congregation at the Report of the spies that had been they were not only discouraged but had Got to search out the Land. and the words it put them into a dreadfull fret against moses and Aaron & against God and when Joshua and Caleb Opposed them and would have Convinced them that their discuragement and murmuring was Causeless they Could not bear it but were about to stone em. all the 10. all the Congregation Bade stone em with stones upon the

___________________________

upon this the Glory of G. appeared it was time for him now to Appear & in the 11. & 12 v. we have an Account of what God says upon this occasion ----------------------

in The words of our text are part of what said in Reply to mose Upon this moses in a most humble and Earnest manner Intercedes as he used to do had been wont to do for the Congregation. & the words of the text are a Part of what G say in the Reply said in Reply to his Intercession. God is so far as it were Overcome by moses's Intercession that he Pardons them as a nation v 20 I have Pardon'd according to thy word. he had Pardoned he would Concede to bring d not to destroy the nation as he had threatend in the 11 & 12 verses and as for that Generation. those [^039-note1] Persons that had murmured & Provoked him God would not Pardon as he he would not as he declares in Our text we may Observe in the words

The expression is abrupt something Else is understood if they shall see the Land. then I am not a God then I dont live . the same is signified that is expressed in the 21 v verse before the text as truly as I live saith the L. all the Earth shall be filled with the Glory of the L. that is I will not suffer the Glory of my majesty to be thus Contemd & trampled on. and again in the 28 v. as truly as truly as I live saith the L as Ye have spoken in mine Ears so will I do unto You

G. had threatend before but not Resolved The expression shows Gods wrath they had so Provoked G. that his wo patience was at end An End he sware in his wrath he is most peremptory and Repeats it again & again. in the v. before the text as truly as I live ---------- .& then in the [^039-note2] text if ye they shall see the Land & again in the 28 v. as truly as I live saith the L. . & again in the 30 v. doubtless ye shall not Come into the L. Concerning which I sware to make you dwell therin & again in the 35. v. I the L. have said it & I will surely do it unto all this Evil Congregation. 3. We may Observe the Reasons why G. is thus Immutably Resolves -------- viz. the number & Repeatedness of their transgressions the 1. the aggravation of their Provocation They have seen my Glory & my miracles which I did in Egypt & in the wiLd. . 2 That this Provocation was after so many others the Repeatedness of their tran they have tempted me now these 10 tim by taking notice of the History that Moses Gives of us we may Observe that this is the 10th Publick transgression act of Rebellion that Perverseness and Rebellion that is mentioned from their Coming out of Egypt. the 1st at the Red sea when they murmured at the Red se Sea Exod 14.10.11 the Second their Gathering murmuring at Marah Exod 15 23.24 the 3d their Gathering their murmuring at manna on the sabbath for that is spoken of & Reproved[^039-note3] taken notice of & Reproved as a Publick act of Rebellion Exod 16. 27 28. G. says upon that occasion how long Refuse ye to Keep my statutes Commandments & my Laws The third fourth The 3d their muring at the Wild of sin Exod 16.1.2. \| The 4th their Gathering of manna on the sab. --- which is taken notice of & Reproved by G. as a Publick act of Rebellion Exod 16 27.28 G. says upon that Occasion how long will it be Refuse ye to keep my Command---- & my Laws. The 5 at Meribah Exod 17. 4 1st &c -- The 6 the making the Golden Calf Exod 32 1 &c The 6 at The 7. at Taberah numb 11.1 The 8. Their Loathing of manna. numb 11 4. The 9th Aarons & Miriams sedition with whom doubtless many of the Congreg. Joind. numb 6.12 1 &c--- . & now the 10th Their murmuring at the Relation of the spies Doc. There is such a thing as mens' Going on to Provoke God by their sins till they have Committed the Last sin that God will bear with before he as it were takes up a Resolution that they never shall be saved. This Rest that God swore the Chil. of Is. should not Enter into is typical of heavenly Rest and Gods thus dealing with the Chil of Israel in the wild with Respect to Canaan is a Representation of his dealing with some wicked men with Respect to Heaven & their Eternal [^039-note4] salvation as is Evident from the Improvement which the Psalmist and the Apostle Paul makes of it to warn men not to do as they did Least that G. should deal with them with Respect to their salvation as he did with that the Chi those murmurers with Respect to the Promised. Land. Thus The Psalmist warns us not to harden our hearts as in the Provocation in the Day of temptation in the wilderness and Enforces his warning by telling us how they G. dealt with them he swore in wrath that they should not Enter into his Rest. Intim Intimating that if we do as they did we shall expose our selves to the like treatment with Respect to God's havenly Rest for it was Long after the Chil of Israel had obtained that temporal Rest as the Apostle Argues in the 3d& 4th Chap. to the Heb. & There the apostle expressly warns Xtians Least to beware Least they Provoke G. to do with them with Respect to heaven as the Child of Is d he dealt with those men with Respect to Canaan as you may observe by the whole drift of these two Chap. to the Heb. & particularly the 11 v. of the 4 Chap. Let us Labour therefore to Enter into that Rest Least any man fall after the same example of unbelief so that tis Evident that as G did with the Chil of Is. wi at this time with Respect to Canaan so he sometimes doth sometimes with wicked men with Respect to their Eternal salvation. 2. God G.od is dreadfully Provoked by mens Continuing to Go on in Going on in ways of wickedness especially under Clear light & while he is using means [^039-note5] with them to Reclaim them. & he many so Provoke him that he as it were Resolves.------- & his Resolution may be dated from some Particular transgression that did as it were seal their damnation. 1. Enquire How .G. may be said to take up a Resolution that a man never shall be saved, and here I an 1st . I Answer negatively G. Cant be Properly said to take up any Resolution in time. That would argue mutability in G. there is nothing new in G. Whatsoever God Purposes he Purposes from all Eternity. hed determined when the Chil of Israel Came out of Egypt & before that that Generation should not see the Land of Canaan. it was in Gods decree then & when they made the Golden Calf tho G. forgave that s upon moses's Intercession & said after that Go up and Possess the Yet it was his Land. But yet God's Decree was the same all along tho the Pillar of Cloud & fire Led them towards Canaan with it God brought em to the borders of it. But yet here God is in Our text G. is Represented as Coming to this Resolves that they shall upon this Transgression of their murmuring at the Report of the spies G. is Represented in s Tho G. be unchangeable is Represented after the manner spoken of after the manner of men as altering his Purposes & taking up new Purposes. So he is said to Repent. so he is Represented as taking up Resolutions so in the 6. of Gen. 6. & 7. verses and it Repented the L. that he had made man on the Earth & it Grieved him at his heart. & the L. said I & the L. said I will destroy man theres his Repentance. & the L said I will destroy man whom I have Created from off the [^039-note6] face of the Earth there is his new Res. & so Gen 8.21. & the L. smelled a sweet savour & the L said in his heart I will not Curse the Ground any more for mens sake. There G. is Re is Represented as taking up a Resolution not to Curse the Ground upon upon a sal Noahs sacrifice. his saying in his heart is the same as the In the Heb way of expressing as his Resolving within himself in our Language. so that G. Cant properly & in strictness be said to take up a a Resolution not to save man upon any sin of theirs. But 2. G. acts as tho he had taken up such a Resolution or he at to acts as men do when they have taken up a Resolution against a thing. and here Particularly with Respect to those whom the doc speaks of some of those that Go on to provoke G by their sins 1. G. from the time that they Committed such a sin finally withdraws from them & witholds the Kindly Influence of his Sp absents himself from them and Refuses to Convict men Ever to Give men saving Repentance of their sins. he witholds from men those Kindly Influences of his Sp that are necessary In order to their salvation none Can be saved according to Gods Immutable Constitution except they experience such Influences of the sp of G. working Grace in their hearts Causing a work of Regeneration. but this G. is provoked to forever to withold. G is so Provoked that he his holy sp never shall so and dwell in their hearts The apostle warns the Xtian Heb not to Commit fornication Least it should be with them as it was [^039-note7] with Esay Esay Esau who for a morsel of meat (for a moments gratification of an appetite) sold his birthright who afterwards found no Place for Repentance Heb 12.16.17. 2. from that time forward G. Refuses to save men tho they seek it and do many things in order to it. They design to be saved but G. Closes them disappoints them have a Great desire to escape hell but G Never will deliver 'em, they design to be saved but G. disappoints em they design to set about the work of their souls at such a time and and such a time but G blasts their designs , they make attempts to sus forsake their sins to sin & to set about their work of Religion in Good Earnest but G. blesses em in their attempt he dont assist em to do as they attempt to Do & prosper 'em in their attempts. They Do many things that they may be saved. but yet they bent blessed in in their Endeavors their Endeavors dont Prosper.. Thus it was with the Chil. of Israel they made attempts to Go up to Canaan after that they had Committed that sin of murmuring at the Report of the spires. as you may see in the 40 verse & onward of the Chap of our text . & they Rose up Early in the morning. (they seem to set about the work with Considerable Earnestness) & Got them up into the top of the mountain saying Lo we be here and will Go up into the Place which [^039-note8] the L. hath Promised for we have sinned . & but moses tells em in the next verse that it shall not Prosper he that & that the L. is not amongst em & that they should be smitten before their Enemies. But yet they ha seemed to have a Great mind to Go (tho before they were for making them a Captain & Returning into Egypt) & so they would Go up notwithstanding but the ark of the Covenant of the L. & moses did not Go with them & the Amalekites Came down & the Canaanites & smote them & Discomfited them Even unto Hormah. Tho they she shed tears about their sins yet G. will utterly Refuse to save em . when moses brought the message from G. the of what he had said of em it is said the People mourned Greatly v. 39. and often they were smitten by the Canaanites they Returned & wept before the L. but the L. would not hearken to their voice nor Give Ear unto them Deut 1.44.45 so the apostle warns Xtians not to Do Commit fornicatin the forementioned Place not to Commit fornication Least it should be with them as with Esay Esau who found no Place for Repentance tho he sought it Carefully with tears. 3. G. finally Leaves them & Gives them up to sin. Tho they it may have fears of damnation and they may have Great terrours of Consc. sometimes their Consciences fright em as tho they were frightened with they have now and then Great stings of Conscience & twinges of Conscience yet they have no Kindly Convictions[^039-note9] they Cant they may be now & then frighted as tho they beheld a spectre so some frightfull spectre Yet they have no Convictions that work Kindly that is that make em set in to forsake all their known sins & in Good Earnest to use set about Using the means for their salvation. They may design to seek set about seeking salvation & project such a thing from time to time yet something satan has Power Given to hinder them one way or other so that they never do it in Good Earnest. They may make attempts & that it they will break off their sins but yet when the temptation Comes their lusts are stir'd up they are Carried away again. so God Gives em to the Power of their lusts they are Car Carried Captive by them & are become meer slaves to them. Conscience from time to time makes opposition but Conscience is wore down. They may Continue seeking and doing many things for a Considerable time but all the while they Indulge some lust in a Greater or lesser degree they never wholly broke off all their known sins & so finally Leaves men & Gives them up to their sins he never Gives them such Kindly Influences & assistances of his Sp. as to Cause them wholly to forsake their wickedness ness. Thus G. did by these murmurers in the wilderness Ps. 81 . 11 . 12. But my 'People' would not hearken to my voice & Israel would none of me so I Gave them up to [^039-note10] their own hearts Lust and they walked in their own Counsels. 4. G. Refuses to hear the Prayers of others Concern for theirm Fr he Refuses to Answer the Pr tho their Godly Fr Friends or ministers Parents or other Friends or ministers Pray for their Conversion & salvation God Refuses to Answer them. Moses Earnestly Interceded for this Evil Rebellious Congregation of Israel & G. heard him so far that he would not destroy the nation but al as for that Evil Generation God would not hear him destroy them. Thus G. said to Jer. 7.16. Therefore Pray not then for this People neither lift up Cry nor Prayer for them neither make intercession to me for I will not hear thee. 5. Ministers are sent to them on that Errand to harden their hearts. Thus when God was Resolved upon the destruction of Judah & Jerusalem he sent Isai. upon this Errand: Isai 6.10. make the heart of this People fat and make their Ears heavy & shut their Eyes Lest they should see with their Eyes & hear with their Ears & understand with their heart & Convert and be healed the means of Grace Prove a savour of death with Respect to them their having Continued under means of Grace is no Argument that G. had has not Resolved that they never shall be saved. for that wicked murmuring Generation whose Carcases fell in the wild the ma [^039-note11] manna descended to em they after that G. had sworn that they should not Enter into his Rest. 6. Sometimes God suddenly takes away mens lives after they have Put an End to Gods Patientce by some Particular Comm after the Commission of that sin. when they have been Going on in sin wretchedness, they at Last do Commit the last sin that G will bear. if now sin from whence he takes up a Resolution that they shall be Damned and soon after G. takes away their lives or sends em to hell that they maynt be kept out of hell any longer. when they are dead Eccles. 7.17 be not over much wicked why shouldest thou die before thy time. G. is some times Revolved to snatch men away out of the T. as being not fit to live & he hastens their destruction in wrath. So Judas. wi Tis Gods manner sometimes thus to deal with wicked men not only under the O.T. but also under the new Annanid Ananias & sapphira were struc struck dead for their sins Herod was Eaten with worms for his wickedness Reasons 1. God doth thus to vindicate his own as he would vindicate his own Glory. G. might Glorify his sovereign & Infinite Grace in their Conversion & pardon. But G. is pleased to Glorify his Justice as well as by his severity on some as well as his mercy on others. and this is [^039-note12] one way of his expressing his wrath whereby he glorifies his Justice. Thus G. said to moses when he Interceded for Israel in the v. before the text as I live sait saith the L. all the Earth ------------

## 141. II Sam. 22:26-27 141.II Sam. 22'26 trans

Jonathan Edwards

Isai 42.21. he will magnify the Law & make it honourable this Chap. This Chap. is a Prophecy of X. & among other things that are declared of him he in this verse is set declared the acceptableness of & sufficiency of his mediation satis faction & Righteousness 2 Sam 22 26 . with the mercifull man thou wilt show thy self mercifull & with the upright man thou wilt show thy self upright . with the Pure thou wilt show thy self Pure & with the froward thou wilt show thy self unsavoury . Thise words are Part of a song that david of Praise that david sang towards the Lanter end of his Reign & life [--] when he Came to be in his old age he had Rest from war . it was to Praise G. that he had in all the wars his wars and in all the dangers he had been Involved in that he had at Length delivered him & appeared on his side against his Enemies david had abundance of Enemies that that sought his Ruin in the Course of life. from the his first being Called from the sheep Cote to Come & stand before saul till the Latter Part of his Reign he had Enemies to Encounter. he was Pers exceedingly Persecuted by Enemies before he Came to the Crown . and afterwards he had wars with all the nations Round about him besides the Great Troubles he met with from within his own dominion & his own Family But however G. was with him in all al his troubles & Dangers he appeared on his side & never suffered his [^041-note1] Enemies to triumph over him & at Last he Gave him the victory over all & he in his old age had his throng throne & his Kingdom in a well established Peace & quietness. david in this Part of his song is Reflecting upon Gods dif ferent dealings with him & with his Enemies & his Righteousness & Equity therein . he takes notice how G had Rewarded him according to his Righteousness & according to his Cleanness in his Eye sight. which Leads to Reflect on on Gods universallv Righteousness & Equity in his dealings with men & Judging of them . he distributes to Every one according to his own practice & prevailing disposition as appeared in his dif ferent dealings with him & with his Enemies .. with the mercifull doc. That G. will deal with all men according to their own temper & Practice This seems to be the design of the words of the words of the text to teach us this & not only that G. deals with men according to their own temper & practice in those Particular In stances here mentioned

G. who is our supream Judge has Placed mankind in the T in such a state that there is a they stand in need one of another they in many things have a mutual dependence. & G. beholds us from heaven & observes how we behave one towards another . he hath Given us Rules to for us to attend in order to one anothers welfare and tells us that according as we treat one another in an observance or neglect of those Rules so we must expect to be treated by himself. math 7. 1 . w he observes what measure we Give to our fellow Creatures & he Gives us the same math 7. 2. with what measure you mete it shall be measured to you again we shall take notice of some Instances 1 G. will be mercifull to those that are mercifull & liber al to those that are so to their fellow Creatures But those that are unmercifull to men shall not be so be [^041-note17] obtain mercy of G. Jonathan Edwards

Ps . 14 . 1. The fool hath said in his heart There is no G. He who has Infinite wisdom. who sits in heaven & from thence Perfectly beholds all things as they are & knows what is wise & what is unwise better than any other what is wisdom & what is folly . has in his holy word stigmatized wickedness as the the wicked as the Greatest fools so that we find 'em there Called fools as tho they were so: in the most eminent manner & so wisdom is used for Righteousness for holiness Commonly in the ss as being synonimous or . exactly of the same signification. The wicked are Called fools in this verse 1. as a General appellation that belonged to them. as they are Called elsewhere as Ps 107 . 17 . fools because of their transgressions & Prov 13 . 19 . it is an abomination to fools to depart from Evil . & 20 a Companion of fools shall be destroyed . & in many other Places. & 2 with a Particular Eye to that Part of their folly here mentioned viz that they say in their hearts --------------- this is one Influence of their strong stupidity & sottishness of their minds . some do suppose that by the expression of saying in their heart --------- is meant chiefly their in their Incli nation . But by heart in ss is often very Commonly meant the whole soul Including the all the faculties . [^045-note1] thus we Read of men pondering things in the heart by which is principally Intended an act of the Understanding and it seems here to be meant of the whole soul for as sin has dominion over the whole soul so atheism is what taints all the faculties . doc. a Principle of Atheism Possesses the hearts of all wicked men Ungodly men. By Atheism is Commonly meant the disbelieving or denying his the Being of a G. and as extending no further than to the und act of the Understanding & the Profession of that act it . but by the word in the doc I would be understood in a sense some thing more extensive, for any kind of Rejecting Renouncing or opposing d The divine existence or the Being of a G. with whatever faculty. all wh which sense we suppose to be Parallel with the expression in the text of saying in the heart there is th No G. & accordingly we shall show 1. That there is a Principle of Speculative atheism or atheism of Jud an atheistical Inclination 2. There is speculative atheism or atheism of Judgmt in Every ungodly . m 3. They have not a disposition Practically to deny G. or to live as if there were no G. I. There is an Atheistical Inclination that Possesses the [^045-note2] Hearts of every ungodly man. i. e they have such an Inclination & nature that it would suit them if there were no G. they have nothing in them that disposes & Inclines them makes them incline that there should be a G. but they Could be Glad if there were none . it would mightily suit & please them if they Could be assur red that there was none. there is such a sp of Enmity in their hearts against G. every thing that they hear of G. is disagreable to em. in their nat natures are entirely Contrary to the nature of G in the first Place they hate the holiness of G. and they hate all the other attributes because this his holiness does as it were Influence them all all the other attributes & actuate all his other attributes as his Power wisdom & mercy. They They Easily Percieve that tis not for Interest [--] that there should be a G. if they there be a G. then they are sensible , that he is their Enemy . unless they take up a wrong opinion of themselves & think themselves to be Gods friends. this belief of a the Being of a G. they easily Pers Percieve would be a thing very much Cross to their strongest Inclinations & appetites . it would disturb them & Create them a Great deal of uneasiness in their pursuit of their lusts to think that there is an almighty being that has them & all things in their hands & that he sees perfectly hates sin & will Revenge it that behold them Continually & sees their hearts & all their secret actions. [^045-note3] This is what they [ ] have they have no Inclination that it should be thus . it is what they Could heartily wish for that they Could be assured it were otherwise that that was no supream being to take notice of their behaviour & Call them to an account they have disposition Enough to Pull G. or dethrone G. or to Kill him if it Lay in their Power . 2 . they ha Ungodly men have all a Principle of Speculative atheism or atheism of Judgmt. tha Possesses the hearts of all ungodly men. the dark natural blindness of the Children of men extends so far as to darken their understandings with Respect to the being of G.. mens Judgmts are naturally & so desparately depraved the Principle of unbelief that is naturally in the hearts extends to Every thing that is divine & not only to it Respects the whole of Religion . they have not [--] only unbelief with Relation to the Sufficiency of X Righteousness to Satisfy for their sins & Recommend them to G. & with Relation to those divine doc. of the Gosp. that Ref about the mediation of X Incarnation & medi ation of X that are so much above the light of nature but they have a in their hearts a Principle of unbelief of the very being of a G. unbelief of the doc & principle of nath natural Relig. & not only own of the very being of a G. Here here we shall take notice of the several ways wherin this atheistical Principle expresses it self But 1 0 shall first Observe that however there is [^045-note4] such a Principle of atheism in all mens yet tis very questionable whether there ever was any man that ever was able fully to satisfy himself that there was no G. There have been many that finding that the belief of the being of a G. did not wo to would not Comfort suit with their sinfull Pursuits or Agree with lusts & which their Carnal Pleasures & delights have Laboured to free themselves from this Incumbrance & and entirely to throw off the Yoke off Religion & Restrai of Religion & to free themselves of all Restraint from the[-] apprehensions of a supream Judge the to Call them to an account . But tis very questionable whether any of them ever so far obtained their end or By studying objecting & Cavilling to free themselves from all sense of the being of G a G. so as to Get Rid of fears & Jealousies & terrifying apprehensions of his being & especially at times. however Perverse & depraved some mens Reason is being blinded by their lusts Pride lusts blinded & misled by their sinfull Prejudices & made headstrong by their Pride. Yet studying & Reasoning is that not the way to make men perfect atheists tho they set themselves about it for thats very End to to object & cavil against the existence & to [---] Ease their own minds of the Burthen of a Jealousy of it . But the likely likeliest way for men to bring them selves to it or to Come as near it as men Can Come is not to Consider at all to Improve- exercise [^045-note5] their Reason as little as ever they Can to & make hast and make themselves every way as much like beasts as lies in their Power to be as thoughtless & In considerate & stup as theyre .& to stupify their minds darken their understandings with beastly Incli Lusts as fast as they Can. that is the Readiest way to arrive at atheism or to arrive at any Considerable Perfection in it. Habakkuk 2. 4. The Just shall live by his Faith. This Proph. had in the foregoing Chap Prophecied of the destruction of the Land by the Chaldeans & upon the Occasion of the Revelation of that destruction & in the Latter Part of the Chap we have a Prayer of the Prophets wh that he made to upon occasion of the Revelation of that destruction. whereby he Prays for the, destruction of those destroyers & for the deliverance of Gods People The same spirit that Reveald to the Prophet that the Chaldeans should Come & destroy the Land & Carry the People into Captivity had also Revealed to him that after a while the Chaldeans themselves should be destroyed & Gods People that they held in Captivity should be deliver'd for at the same time that the medes & Persians destroyed Babilon Cyrus Proclaimed liberty to the Jews. & this moved the Prophet Earnestly to Pray for the accomplishmt & hastning of it . beginning with the 12 v. of the Preceeding Chap. at art not thou from Everlasting O L. my G & when the Prophet has done his Prayer he tells us in the begin of this Chap that he will stand upon his watch & set him upon the tower to wait & watch for an Answer. & to see what the L. will say in ans answer to him. [^049-note1] & G. answers him by Comma directing him to write the vision & make it Plain upon tables that he may Run that Readeth it . By the vision is meant the Prophecy of the destruction of Chaldea & the Consequent deliverance of his Captives which we have in this Chap beginning with the 5.v & G. assures the Proph that that which he had Prayed for was for an appointed time . & that at the End the vision he had had of it would speak & would not lie & Bids him tho it tarry yet to wait for it for it will surely Come it will not tarry . ho shoul however unlikely the thing might seem & h appear & however Long the time might seem to wait with faith & Patience. Upon this Come in these words of this verse behold his soul that is lifted up is not upright in him but the Just shall live by his faith. the seeming Improbabi ty of the accomplishmt of this Prophecy would be a [---] trial of Persons faith . they that were not upright & sincere when they see the thing delayed & saw no prospect of Probability of any accomplishmt would Give over any expectation of it & would say that the Prophecy was but a vain delusion & li & the like but that those that were truly Just they would not be discouraged . th they would wait for it still tho it tarried & tho their appeared very little [^049-note2] was but a very little appearance of any such thing yet they would not Let Go their hold. Gods Promise would hold them Up Up . their hope & Comfort & would not still but it would live their Encourage ment in a way of Obedience that they drew from this Promise would not die still but would be up upheld & live to the End. doc . That thos the Just live by faith saints do live by Faith The Greatest distinction that there is Among men is of saints & sinners Regenerated & Carnal men there is a vast difference between them in their hearts & in their lives they live a life tha the Godly live a life that the natural men are Utter strangers to & that is as of a nature Kind exceeding Remote from that which they live & Contrary to i as fa as heaven is from Earth & as Contrary as light is to darkness the the so Great a difference often times is not visible in our me for the life of a saint is hidden life . the world sees not wha from what vital Principle it is that they live and what it is they live upon what and for what Ends they live nor do they see those vital acts that & the are the main exercises of their spiritual life. but hereby thei life is described by one main Character of it. viz that they live by faith 1 Enq. what life of the saint it is that is by faith [^049-note3] 1. w Concerning the nature of Faith . 2 What life of the saint it is by faith . 3. how far & in what Respects this life of theirs is by faith. I Enq. is Concerning the nature of faith. how faith in ss is sometimes to be taken in a more General & sometimes in a more Particular sense Restrained & Particular according to the more General or & Particular object. 1 it may be Considerd as it Respects G. in the whole of of our Concern with him either in the affairs of our souls or bodies. & so tak Considered thus it may be thus defind It is the Acquiescence of the soul in the divine sufficiency & truth in all Concerns between him & us. thus it is by faith that we truly believe that G. made the Θ & that he is our autho tis by faith that we believe the histories of the flood & destruction of sodom the bringing the Chil. of Israel out of Egypt. so tis by faith that we believe that G. is able to deliver us from all adversity & to make us happy . tis p if we are Going forth to war against our temporal Enemies tis by faith that we believe that G is able to help & to Give us victory it was by faith that Calab & Joshua thought that G. was able to Give em victory over the Giants of Canaan. & that he Could deliver into their hands the Cities that were defended fortified with walls up to heaven . it was by faith that shadrach. ---------- believed that God was able to deliver them out of Nebuchadnezars [^049-note4] hand & from the Power of the burning fiery furnace it was by faith that those that were heald of their diseases by X believed that he was able to heal them . Tis by faith that Gods Promises of temporal Good are believed . it was by faith that those mentioned in our text believed that the time should Come when G. would deliver the Chil of Israel from their Babilonish Cap. so it is by faith that threatnings are believed it was by faith that the true Xtians that were in Jeru salem before its destruction believed that the destruction of it was right when they saw Jerusalem Compas Compassed with armies and those other signs that X Gave them But then 2. Faith may be Consider'd in a more Restrained sense as it Respects J. X in the Concern of the sal vation of our souls . & so it may be thus defined The acquiescence of the whole soul to X. J. as a Real sufficient & excellent Saviour this dont specifically differ from the other it is not properly another distinct sort of faith but is Comprized in it it is a particular sort Compri Contained in that more General the faith t we explained under the former head in is faith Considerd in its more General nature & that which with Respect to its General Object faith as we have descr what we now are speaking of is Faith Considered only with Respect to a particular Object and exercise . & Relating to a particular[^049-note5] Concern th of ours viz the Concern of our salvation by J. X. Faith in this sense is a Clo Closing with J. X. eve & with then his salvation with every faculty of the soul . there the apprehension Recieves him X in his & his salvation with the beauty. agreableness suitableness & Glory thereof is apprehended & understood. the Judgmt Closes with it the soul believes & is convinced that X is a Real saviour that the tidings of his salvation is true & Certain & the X is a sufficien soul is Convinced that X is a sufficient saviour able to save to the uttermost that his satisfaction is valid & his Righteousness aceptable with G. upon our account. The will and Inclination Closes with it the prevailing Inclination of the soul in is towards X & to his way of salvation the man soul Chooses it before all others whatsoever he hates his own Righ. & loves the Righ. of X his heart is united to X & his Rest in him & as desiring no other saviour or Portion The heart Closes with X with all the affection & desire & delight he that believes Rejoices in X Jesus & has not Confidence in the flesh. II Enq. what Life of the saint it is that is by with Respect to what Life of the saint it is that it is said he lives by faith. Ans the life of the soul here Let it be Consider'd that Life denotes two things . it denotes something of Perfection & something of Enjoyment. Life denotes Good but there are but these two kinds of Good Good of excellency or perfection & Good of Enjoymt It denotes something of Perfection when [^049-note6] we speak of life we have Respect to something that is the Perfection of that that lives whereby it is a more Perfect kind of being than that which that does not live. It denotes something of Enjoymt Life Carries in it something denotes something desireable something that it is a happiness to have as an Enjoymt or a desirea ble thing to have or & something that it would be a misery to be deprived of . death Carries in it something doleful Calamitous & dolefull such Ideas as these are naturally excited by the Common & ordinary use of the word life & especially are do the word Carry these things in its meaning as used in the ss. Therefore when a spiritual being Possesses the proper perfection of hi its nature & excellency of its nature or & also Enjoys an that Good & happiness for which it is suited & Prepared by nature & designed by nature then may it be said to be in a state of life in a ss. sense. & so long as that Perfection or excellency & that being is up maintained & preserved in that the Possession of that Perfection and that Enjoyment so Long may its be life be said to be Uphold so long doth it Continue to live. in a ss. sense But when a spiritual being is wholly destitute of the Proper Perfection of its nature or to has so much odiousness & deformity as to be as bad or worse than nothing . & to be without the proper Enjoymts [^049-note7] of its nature so as to be bad or wo or to have the Contrary misery so that as to be in a state as bad or worse than that of nonexistence . then is a spirit or soul in a state of death. nothing es else Can be Understood by the Life or Death of a spiritual substance but this. when we say that a spirit is in a state of death, it Cant be meant that it is in a state of dissolution for there is no dissolution of a spirit nor Can it be meant that it is in a state of nothing or nonexistence for that is no state at all & besides there never has been nor ever will be any such thing as the turning of any sp. into nothing. That which we Commonly Call the death of men is not the death of the soul or spirit the tis the death of the body . the body is deprived of all its natural Perfection as a human body, of all its Powers & Capacities of Enjoymt action & also of all its Enjoymt and all its Powers of Enjoying any thing. But in this that we have now said Consists the life of a soul or sp. in viz in the Possession of its proper pe being endowed with its proper excellency & & in enjoying its Proper Good. so that its being should be not be worse but better than nothing & its state more eligible than nonexistence & this I believe distin description of the life of a soul or spirit I believe if examined will be found very much to agree with the ss use of the word when [^049-note8] speaking of the life of souls or spirits.

herin Consists what we Call spiritual life . viz in the souls being Endowed with that holiness & Image of G. & those spiritual Principles of action wherin Consists the Proper Perfection & excellency of the soul of man . & to the souls being having with in it self a foundation and spring of spiritual Peacli Peace Comfort & Joy which is the proper happiness of the soul. the Good that was fitt made Designed & titled by nature for. & herin also Consists Eternal life. only brought to its Perfection. when the soul is Endowed with these exc excellencies that are the proper excellency of its nature in & Enjoys this happiness in perfection then it Enjoys Eternal life. & spiritual & Eternal death Consists in the Contrary & it with Respect to this Life that the Just are said to live by faith. But we shall show more Particularly how in answering to the following Enq. viz IIIdly In what Respects this Life of the saints is by Faith. it is so these two ways . viz as a Qualifi cation an as a means. 1. as a Qualification faith is that qualification where by they become Entitled unto life according to the tenour of the Cov. of Gr. Joh. 3. 36 he that believeth on the son hath Everlasting life & he that believeth not the son shall not see life This is the qualification which G. has a primary Respect to in Justifying men in delivering of them from Eternal[^049-note9] death & bestowing upon them Giving them a title to Eternal life we as we Come into the Θ are born under obligation to Eternal death but X hath Purchased Eternal life for us & tis by fai this is the Qualification that G. has Respect to in us in his looking upon us as being in X & so Imputing to Us his Righ. & Giving us a ti title to that Eternal life which he has purchased which Consists in perfect holiness & happiness in the Enj Conformity union with & Enjoymt of G. which the Holy sp the with that is Given in this Θ with his sanctifying & Comforting Influences is the beginni Earnest of. 2. Faith is the means of the life of the Just . [-] This is the means by which the life of their souls is obtaind & sustained 1 Faith is the means by which the life of the souls of the saints is obtained . 1 By this they Recieve Grace & holiness from J.X Faith is that by which the soul is united to X & tis by virtue of the union with X that the soul Recieves his holy & Gracious Influences . faith is the proper uniting act of the soul towards J. X whereby it Recieves & Closes with him . & being hereby united to X believers become his members & he is their head to Communicate his Gracious Influences vital Influences we are naturally branches of a wild olive by faith [^049-note10] we are Ingrafted into X & become branches of him & so we Recieve from him sap & nourishmt so that tis by faith that we Recieve principles derive holiness fr & Grace from our head J. X. and Re cieve supplies of the holy Gh. & his sanctifying In fluences & of his fullness Recieve & Grace & for Grace by this they bring forth fruits. faith works by love 2. Faith is the spring of spiritual Peace, hope Comfort & hope. beli it is a means not only of of th hol the perfection & spiritual excellency of the saints Which Consists in Grace & holiness but of that Enjo those Enjoymts that w that are suited to our nature & for which we were designed. a fallen Creature Can Recieve no spiritual Comfort & or Joy but by faith . the Eunuch when he had believed he went out his way Rejoicing Acts 8. 38. 39 . & Rom. 15. 13. we Read of all Joy & Peace in Believing. & to the like purp purpose I Pet . 1. 7. 8 in whom tho now ye see him not yet believing ye Rejoice with Joy unspeakable & full of Glory . Those things which the Xtian lives upon for whence he Recieves the Comfort of his life are unseen & some of them future & therefore it must be by faith that he must fetch Comfort from them a Xtian Cant live up on things in while upon Earth Cant live upon things in heaven unless it be by faith he Cant feed upon that that is Purely spiritual[^049-note11] so as to be nourished & Refreshed by it un less it be by faith. he Cant make future things Present to him so as to live upon em & have the Comfort of em any other way than by faith tis by faith that the soul has Peace of Consc.- that it is deliver'd from a sense of Guilt & fear of wrath it is by a sense of the sufficiency of Xs satisfaction . & b a belief of the truth of the offers of Reconciliation by him Tis by faith that the believer has Joy in his a sense of Gods Glory & the Loveliness of X and a sense of his Interest in those Glorious objects. the Glory of G is som seen & our Interest in him as a portion is known by faith Tis by faith that the saint Recieves Comfort in a sense of Gods love by that he believes the Gracious declaration of his love to those that are in X that are Given in his word. Tis by faith t Faith is the spring of that Joyfull hope which the believer hath of future Glory. 2 Tis by faith that the life of the Xtian is maintaind under the trials & difficulties that he meets with if the heart of the saint if it were not for if the heart of the Xtian were not up supported by faith there are many times when it would be overcome & would yield the Case it would faint & die Give up the Ghost Ps 27. 13. I had fainted un less I had believed to see the salvation of the L Goodness of the L. if it were not for faith many a time would the [^049-note12] saint sink & be overwhelmed in the flood. tis by faith that they are Enabled to wake walk upon the water. it was from the failing of Peters faith that he began to sink . tis by faith that Xtians Can Go through the fire & the flame not kindle upon them. tis Tis by faith that the Graces of the Xtian are maintained in exercise under opposition that temp tations are over come and Enemies Resisted it is by the shield of faith ma in times of darkness & difficulty the saints would leave off following G. they would be discouraged in ob serving of him were they no held up by faith . if they did not not trust in Gods declarations & promises they would surely Give out. so tis by faith that Comfort is maintained under in sorrows & trou troubles of the world . the Xtian he sees light in darkness he has inward Peace in outward storms Inward Joy in outward trouble & sorr sorrow but it is by faith whereby he depends upon G. & looks to J. Applicat. 1. hereby we may try try our faith whether it be of the Right Kind. we may examine whether our faith be such a faith as we Can live by. there is a false & Counterfeit faith some Imagine that they believe the Gospel & that they have a dependence upon G. & are lovers upon X alone for salvation. but [^049-note13] it is but a shadow without a substance it is not a faith that they Can live do or Can live by it is not a faith that brings with a Change of nature & that sanctifies them & makes them partakers of Gods holiness it is not a faith that so unites their hearts to J. X. or that they derive from him his temper & spirit it is not a faith that they walk by that is such a living Gr vital Principle as Influences their outward behaviour in the General Course of their lives & Causes them to bring forth fruits of Righteousness Tis not a faith that upholds them in a way of obedience & following J. Exod. 20 .24 ---------- In all Places where I Record my name I will Come unto thee and I will bless thee. God is now speaking unto moses out of the thick darkness from mount sinai. we Read in the foregoing Chap of the first Coming unto this mountain after their Coming out of Egypt . and how moses went up to God to into there that to the mount. and how that G. orderd the attendance of the Congregation at the foot of the mountain to hear him speak to them see the tokens of his Presence & majesty & to hear him speak to them & to Recieve the Law at his mount . and and then God Came down in in a very awfull & terrible manner upon the mountain and spoke to the People with and on a mighty voice in the hearing of all the Congr. and first deliv Gave them spoke to them the ten Commandments . with a very Loud and mighty voice. which was attended wi with mount sinai being altogether in a smoke and with the appearance of devouring fire. and with terrible thunders & lightning and the moun tain & the Ground about it Quaking exceedingly shaking Quaking & exceedingly & the voice of a sound of a trum pet exceeding Loud . besides the awfull majesty of the voice of G. which spake to them . so that all the peo people that were in the Camp trembled . and were exceedingly afrighted. it was more than they Could bear thus to hear G. speaking to them. they therefore said to moses as in the 19.v. speak thou with us and we will hear but Let not G. speak with us Least we die. upon this the People stood afar off and moses drew near [^050-note1] to the thick darkness where G. was to hear G. speak to him and that he might speak his word to him to the People and Carry Gods message to them. and our text is Part of what G. now speaks to him to declare to the People he tells moses . when moses drew near G. tells him in what way he would m not be worshipped & in what way he would be worshipped by the people. and first forewarns them of making other Gods or worship ping him by Images. 1. for G. to bestow his Grace without Any Appointed means Tis Agreable to Gods wisdom to order Gover Govern the moral world as he does the natural world by stated means
